title: Implement Trie (Prefix Tree)
hints: insert, search, and startsWith all walk character by character from a shared root - what tree structure lets sibling words share the path they have in common?
define a node as a map from character to child node, plus a flag for 'a word ends here'
insert: walk from the root, creating a child node for any character that doesn't exist yet, then mark the final node's flag
search: walk from the root following each character; if you ever can't find a needed child, return false immediately, otherwise return whether the final node's flag is set
startsWith is almost identical to search, except you don't care about the final flag - just whether the walk completes without falling off the trie
commonMistakes: confusing search (must end exactly on a word) with startsWith (just needs the path to exist)
forgetting to mark the end-of-word flag on insert, making search always return false
not handling repeated inserts of the same word, though this should be harmless if the trie is built correctly

content.problemStatement:
You're given a single space-delimited sequence of operations to run
against an initially empty trie (prefix tree). Each token has the form
"op:argument":

- `insert:word` - adds word to the trie
- `search:word` - checks whether word was previously inserted exactly
- `startsWith:prefix` - checks whether any inserted word starts with prefix

**Simulate the tokens in order on the trie, and return a list containing
the result of every "search" and "startsWith" operation (1 for true, 0
for false), in the order they occurred.**

"insert" tokens produce no output and should be skipped in the result
list.
constraints: word and prefix consist only of lowercase English letters
notes: search or startsWith called before any insert
a word that is a strict prefix of another inserted word (e.g. insert 'app' then 'apple')

sampleTestCases.input: ops = "insert:apple search:apple search:app startsWith:app insert:app search:app"
sampleTestCases.explanation: after inserting "apple": search:apple=1 (exact match), search:app=0 (not inserted as a full word yet), startsWith:app=1 (apple starts with app); after inserting "app": search:app=1

sampleTestCases.input: ops = "insert:cat insert:car insert:card search:cat search:ca startsWith:ca startsWith:cars"
sampleTestCases.explanation: "ca" was never inserted as a full word (search:ca=0), but cat/car/card all start with "ca" (startsWith:ca=1); no word starts with "cars"
the trie is empty, so nothing can be found

optimal.time: O(m) per operation, where m is the length of the word or prefix involved
optimal.pattern: a real trie: each node holds a map from character to child node, plus a boolean marking whether a word ends there

bruteForce.approach: keep a plain list of inserted words; for search do an exact-match scan of the list, for startsWith scan the list checking each word's prefix
bruteForce.time: O(n * m) per query, where n is the number of inserted words and m is word length
bruteForce.space: O(n * m) to store the words
